pr_title: feat: how-to pop-up in short sections (#10)
copilot_review_summary: Copilot review: skipped by config/flag (no .vt/vt.config.yaml in this repo, so review.copilot_integration is not enabled). Visual E2E: no ui-visual-reviewer agent; covered by the #10 specs at 320×568/360/390/1280/844×390 and the before/after screenshots in validaciones/shell_generator/10. Verification pass: not run (no C/S findings); M1's recommended fix changes spec decision D6 / FR-011, checked by hand against the template and spec before posting. Security reviewer: no C/S findings (compile-time strings through {{ }} interpolation only; no innerHTML, URL or new dependency). Reviewers: 3 role-scoped `reviewer` instances (security, quality, documentation). Reviewed head: 34ba52a.

findings.title: Screen readers hear "Abre y mueve los sliders…" with nothing after "Abre"
findings.description: The ⚙ is `aria-hidden`, so the spoken Parámetros section is "Parámetros · Abre y mueve los sliders para cambiar tu caracol." and never says what to open. The #10 wording spec pins that exact spoken string. FR-011/D6 assumed the section title covers it, but the title is read before the sentence, not in it.

A.approach: Replace `aria-hidden` on `.howto-gear` with `role="img"` and `[attr.aria-label]` = `GUIDE_GAME_PARAMETERS_TITLE`, so it is read "Abre Parámetros y mueve…"; update the spoken-text spec and amend FR-011/D6.
A.rationale: The standard labelled-glyph pattern. The visible text is unchanged, and it reuses an approved string.

B.approach: Keep `aria-hidden` and reword to "Abre el menú Parámetros (⚙) y mueve…".
B.rationale: The sentence stands on its own, but it changes the approved visible wording.

C.approach: Leave it and record the trade-off in D6.
C.rationale: No change, but screen readers keep the broken sentence.

findings.title: The #31 paragraph spec now pins the count 7, duplicating the #10 order spec
findings.description: 'keeps the how-to text as paragraphs' (#31) asserts `length` 7 and all-P; the #10 'opens on load…' spec already pins the seven children by id. Any added paragraph fails two specs.

A.approach:
Keep only the #31 guarantee: at least one child, and every child a

.
A.rationale: Each spec guards one thing; the #10 spec owns the order and count.

B.rationale: The #10 spec covers it, but #31's intent (paragraphs, not labels) would lose its own name.

findings.title: The five section titles are written out twice in the #10 specs
findings.description: The same five-title array appears in the bold-titles spec and the book-button spec.

A.approach: Hoist `const TITLES = [...]` into the describe and use it in both.
A.rationale: One list to edit when a section changes.

B.approach: Compare the reopened titles with the ones read on first load.
B.rationale: No constant needed, but the first read has to be captured before closing.

findings.title: The goal and closing paragraphs have no id, so the order spec mixes ids and classes
findings.description: Sections are identified by id, the goal and closing by class, so the spec needs `p.id || p.className`.

A.approach: Add ids `howto-goal` and `howto-closing` (keeping the classes) and assert on `p.id`.
A.rationale: Uniform, readable assertion; ids already name the sections.

B.rationale: Also uniform, but the sections' ids are already used by other specs.

findings.title: The layout spec checks every section twice, and the right-edge loop is near-vacuous
findings.description: `[...sections(), ...body().children]` repeats the sections, since they are body children. The scrollWidth checks are the real overflow guard.

B.rationale: Relies only on the scrollWidth checks.

findings.title: The 'text scrolling between them' spec never checks that the text overflows
findings.description: It asserts overflow-y auto/scroll and that the ✕ and ¡A jugar! are on screen, but not `scrollHeight > clientHeight`, so if the text fits, the scroll part tests nothing.

A.approach: Assert the body really overflows at the sizes where it does (measure; at least 320×568), and word the title to match.
A.rationale: Makes the test exercise the case FR-007 worries about.

B.approach: Rename to 'keeps ✕ and ¡A jugar! on screen'.
B.rationale: Honest title, but it doesn't strengthen the test.

findings.title: "Nuevo juego y Compartir" re-types the two guide titles
findings.description: `LABEL_HOWTO_NEW_GAME_SHARE_TITLE` repeats `GUIDE_GAME_NEW_GAME_TITLE` and `GUIDE_GAME_SHARE_TITLE` and can drift from them.

A.approach: Compose it in the template: `{{GUIDE_GAME_NEW_GAME_TITLE}} y {{GUIDE_GAME_SHARE_TITLE}}`.
A.rationale: No duplicate, but it puts Spanish ("y") in the template.

B.approach: Keep the string and add a spec asserting that it contains both guide titles.
B.rationale: Catches drift, and all copy stays in AppStrings.

findings.title: The bold check depends on the browser reporting font-weight '700'
findings.description: `<strong>` is `bolder`; Chrome reports 700 today, but a font-weight on the paragraph would change the number without the text looking less bold.

B.rationale: Stable in the only browser the specs run in.

C.approach: Only check the tag is STRONG.
C.rationale: Weaker; wouldn't catch a CSS reset.

findings.title: howToPlayButtonClick() is a one-liner beside the inline (closed) binding
findings.description: It only sets `howToOpen = false`, the same as `(closed)`. That matches the named-handler style of the other footers.

A.rationale: Consistent with the other footer handlers, and the comment explains why it's enough.

B.rationale: One less method, but it breaks the pattern.

C.rationale: One close path, but (closed) serves every close.

findings.title: The Deployment Started comment says 4 tasks in 2 waves; 6 tasks in 6 waves were built
findings.description: The plan's waves group the work in 2 while tasks.json has W0–W5, so the issue thread shows 4/2 then 6/6 at "Wave 5/6".

A.approach: Add a line under the plan's Waves (archive + plan comment) saying tasks.json splits them into 6 waves.
A.rationale: Explains the jump without editing the automated comment.

findings.title: The plan's Data Model lists LABEL_HOWTO_PARAMETERS, which doesn't exist
findings.description: It was built as `LABEL_HOWTO_PARAMETERS_BEFORE` / `_GEAR` / `_AFTER`, and the hedge under the table doesn't name them.

A.approach: Replace the row with the three built constants and state what was built (archive + plan comment).
A.rationale: The plan matches the code a reader will grep for.

findings.title: Spec and PR predict playButtonClick and a CSS change; neither exists
findings.description: The built method is `howToPlayButtonClick()`, and there is no CSS change in the diff.

A.approach: Name `howToPlayButtonClick` and "CSS: none needed" in the spec (archive + comment); replace Predicted Files with the actual files in the PR body.

B.rationale: The spec keeps the stale name.

findings.title: Nothing says the before/after screenshots exist or what is still pending
findings.description: FR-010/SC-005 require before and after shots at 390/1280. T006 mentions only the after shots, although howto-before-390/1280 and howto-after-* exist in validaciones/shell_generator/10.

A.approach: State in the PR body which before/after shots exist and that owner approval on #10 is pending.

C.rationale: Weakens the gate the owner asked for.

findings.title: The spec's sizes omit 320×568, which the specs also test
findings.description: The layout specs run 320×568 (no sideways scroll plus ✕/¡A jugar! reachable), but FR-007/US4/VM-008/009 list only 360/390/1280/844×390.

A.approach: Add 320×568 to FR-007, US4, VM-008/009 (archive + spec comment) and the PR Test Plan.
A.rationale: The spec states what is verified.

C.approach: Mention it only in the PR Test Plan.
